diagnosis.root_cause: Two active CRM records are assigned to the same physical ONU slot EPON0/4:17, with different ONU line IDs/MACs. Only one ONU can occupy the slot, creating a provisioning and identity conflict even though the currently responding ONU is online.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds with online=1, Auth, and Finish, so the subscriber is currently online.
RX power is normal at about -20.9 dBm, TX power is normal at about +2.38 dBm, and the seven-day optical readings are stable.
TX bias current remains within the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range, so there is no evidence of laser degradation.
Distance is constant at 134, so there is no fibre path change or distance fault.
The OLT answers ping, SNMP, and OID queries; its CPU, memory, and temperature are near healthy baselines.
All visible peers on EPON0/4 are online and healthy, excluding a shared PON, splitter, port, or OLT outage.
The customer has two sessions in 24 hours with long durations, which is normal and does not indicate session flapping.
RADIUS exists, matches CRM, and the expected VLAN 1044 is present, so this is not an authentication or VLAN provisioning fault.
The duplicate_slot_conflict record explicitly shows two active CRM line IDs assigned to EPON0/4:17, which is an invalid one-slot/two-ONU assignment and is the only direct fault evidence.

remediation.action: Audit the two CRM records for EPON0/4:17, identify the physically installed ONU, and remove or correct the stale/incorrect record. Ensure the surviving line ID, ONU MAC, RADIUS identity, and OLT slot binding match, then resynchronize provisioning and verify both CRM and OLT state.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two active CRM records place different ONU MACs on EPON0/4:17. A slot holds exactly one ONU, so one record is stale. The live probe returns a single device, and its MAC matches the subject record, identifying the other as the leftover.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists two active customers on EPON0/4:17 with different ONU MACs
A PON slot holds exactly one ONU, so this state is physically impossible
The live probe of that slot returns a single responding device
The probe's optical values match the subject record's cached reading of -20.88 dBm
RADIUS holds a consistent entry for the subject with normal sessions and traffic
The second record therefore does not correspond to an installed device and is stale
The optical layer is healthy and neither customer is experiencing a service fault
This is a record defect of the same class as the 644 such interfaces in the estate

expected_escalation.review_reason: One of two CRM records on this slot is stale; deleting the wrong one disconnects a live customer

distractors: Nothing is failing and no customer has complained
Both records are marked active and look equally legitimate in CRM
